analysis.title: Investing across scenarios: Strategies for every market environment (Global risk radar)
key_insights: UBS CIO House View base case: continued AI capex strength, a resilient US economy, global fiscal spending and strong credit creation support earnings and markets. The S&P 500 is expected to reach 8,400 by June 2027, with major equity indices about 10% higher.
The Fed hiked 25 basis points in September after hawkish comments from Fed Chair Warsh. UBS now expects two more hikes by mid-2027, then cuts resuming in late 2027.
Bull case (25%): inflation normalizes ahead of schedule on AI productivity gains and faster oil flow normalization, letting the Fed hold rates. S&P 500 around 9,500 by June 2027.
Bear cases total 25%. An 'AI bear market' (10%) takes the S&P 500 as low as 5,500 by June 2027 if AI investment slows or returns fail to materialize. Central banks would then cut rates aggressively.

A 'Yield reset' scenario (15%) has higher energy prices and renewed inflation, possibly amplified by heavy sovereign and corporate bond issuance, forcing markets to price even higher rates. S&P 500 around 7,000 by June 2027, with equities and bonds both under pressure.
Base case assumes Strait of Hormuz traffic resumes gradually despite setbacks. Brent should trade sideways in the coming months and retreat slightly by mid-2027.
US growth is expected near 2% in both 2026 and 2027. Europe and parts of Asia are expected to see below-trend growth from reduced energy flows.

Downside mitigation: replace part of direct equity holdings with capital preservation strategies, add commodities, and shift toward high-quality government and investment grade bonds and select alternatives. VIX near 18 is not stretched by historical standards, and higher rate expectations since the US-Iran conflict began may give attractive terms on these strategies.
Base case return enhancement: use structured investment strategies to boost yield, and reallocate cash and low-yielding bonds into UBS 'Messages in Focus' high-conviction ideas.
Upside participation: increase exposure to growth assets, use leverage or upside-focused structured products within risk limits, and rebalance and take profits rather than chasing past winners.
